@Rado Kirov said:

(hopefully on topic) Does anyone have a very large scale OSS autoformalization project in flight (or quickly spin one up) and interested in pooling our collective 7 days of fable access for collaboration? I imagine a lot of folks will use it for new math results, but I would love to use some of my limitted access to advance formalization somehow.

Here is a challenge, prove that the derived solidification of the free light condensed abelian group on a CW complex computes singular homology: https://github.com/dagurtomas/LeanCondensed/blob/master/LeanCondensed/Projects/DerivedSolidCWHomology.lean

It involves actual condensed mathematics, as well as some general homological algebra and topology.

I only have a small Claude subscription so I assume my Fable access will quickly be eaten up, but I'd be happy to see others work on autoformalizing this
@Dagur Asgeirsson is it possible to make a self-contained file for https://lean-lang.org/eval/

It would be quite long, concatenating code from several files that currently live in LeanCondensed, and it would contain some definitions that depend on sorries on the way to the result. Is that acceptable for lean-eval?
Yes, if you can state a definition and universal properties with sorry. The Jacobian challenge is on lean-eval, for example.
Ok, I will prepare a lean-eval PR
Hmm, the linkifier seems to generate the wrong link here: https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval/pull/471
Obviously, anyone working on this should start by telling their agent to look at https://github.com/dagurtomas/LeanCondensed where significant progress on the early sorries already exists

@Dagur Asgeirsson thanks for pointing this OSS effort, sadly I overestimated how little Fable tokens come with Max, and how quickly it uses them up. So I spent it on a rerun of Jacobian modulo a 300 line cheatsheet .md and I am already out until Sunday.
